Right: one miniature per triad, its three nodes in the accent color and the fourth faded, labeled with the id triple returned: (1, 2, 3), (1, 2, 4), (1, 3, 4), and (2, 3, 4), the 4 ways to choose 3 of 4 nodes." width="100%"} Returns all $\binom{n}{3}$ triples of nodes, each standing for the triad it induces. Combine with `triad_type()` to examine individual triads, or use `triads_by_type()` to group them. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Every triple of node IDs, in ascending order. (NetworkX yields the induced subgraphs instead.) ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Combinations of the node IDs, $O(n^3)$ triples. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#ab206c07 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) len(g.all_triads()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
